subject: Expansion + Hardware regrade proposal for Dedicated pool — performance-per-dollar analysis
messages:
From: Sylvia Brooks <sylvia.brooks@novafin.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase questions for Dedicated pool

Karthik —

Our renewal window is approaching (Nov 15). We want to extend the dedicated pool term to 12 months and increase committed capacity from 16 A100 GPUs to 32 GPUs. Before we lock the numbers in, procurement asked whether a hardware regrade to H100 or L40S is possible in this renewal and how that would affect throughput and unit economics.

Key asks:
- If we move from A100 -> H100, what is expected throughput uplift for our RLHF + chat workloads (median seq len ~512 tokens)?
- If we pick L40S as a cheaper alternative, how does perf-per-dollar compare?
- Can Redwood provide throughput guarantees (tokens/sec per pool) and a canary plan for the hardware swap?

We can run a quick call with your team next week if that helps.

Thanks,
Sylvia Brooks
Director, ML Platform
Nova Financial

(External: please share any perf docs or cost tables)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Brooks <sylvia.brooks@novafin.com>, Tom Harrington <tom.h@novafin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity increase questions for Dedicated pool

Sylvia / Tom —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: yes — we can regrade the pool at renewal, and we have two recommended paths depending on cost vs latency priorities. I attached a compact proposal and a backup workbook with the econ assumptions (attachment: renewal_proposal_v2.pdf, hw_econ_backup.xlsx).

High-level summary here:
- Option A: H100 regrade (recommended if lowest latency matters). On our benchmarks for production chat with 512 token median, a single H100 (house kernel set) delivers ~1.7x token throughput vs an A100 and sustains lower tail latency at 99th pct. Per-GPU hourly cost assumed in the workbook: A100 $7,200/month equivalent, H100 $10,800/month equivalent. Net perf-per-dollar improvement depends on batching (we see ~1.45x perf-per-dollar vs A100 for your workload at observed batching).

- Option B: L40S regrade (best cost-performance balance). L40S delivers ~1.25x throughput vs A100 for chat inference but has memory/layout tradeoffs that give better quantization density. Equivalent monthly cost assumed: L40S $8,900/month. Perf-per-dollar vs A100 at your observed profile: ~1.6x (less tail latency improvement compared to H100, but lower incremental cost).

Throughput guarantees and canary plan: we can commit a throughput SLA per pool (tokens/sec) for the reserved capacity with a 5% credit band and a staged canary where we migrate 2 GPUs to new class, validate tail latency and KV cache hit behavior for 72 hours, then expand to 20% of the pool before full cutover. I've looped Marissa for renewal/legal and Marcus for compute ops for the canary specifics.

If you prefer, we can put numbers into a 12-month commitment comparison (total TCO, monthly burn, and tokens-per-dollar) and share an exec one-pager.

Next steps: call Wed 10/21 10:00am PT?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(attachment: renewal_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF))

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + capacity increase questions for Dedicated pool — internal ops notes

Karthik — forwarding the ask and Karthik's summary. Internal points for the canary + contract:

1) Canary cadence: Marcus, propose 2x GPUs (of new class) for 72h validation, then 6x for one week, then 20% of pool for 7 days before full regrade. We should capture KV cache hit rates, cold-start latency, and failure injection results.

2) SLA sizing: Neha, can you confirm we can offer a tokens/sec SLO that maps to a 32-GPU H100 pool with a 98% availability commitment + 5% credit if breached? If H100 backs out, what fallback to L40S or A100 would look like and pricing impact.

3) Pricing delta: we need the hw_econ_backup.xlsx updated with an incremental-per-token comparison and a blended cost for hybrid regrade (e.g., 24 H100 + 8 L40S) — that significantly changes perf-per-dollar. Marcus, please add operational runbook steps for partial regrade.

On canary docs: I created a short plan and attached it (attachment: canary_plan.md).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Renewals Operations
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Brooks <sylvia.brooks@novafin.com>, Tom Harrington <tom.h@novafin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Final proposal and next steps — 12mo term, 32 GPUs (hybrid H100/L40S)

Sylvia / Tom —

Thanks for the call last week — appreciate the clear constraints (latency for high-priority models, cost for lower-traffic models). Based on the discussion and the internal validation, here is the recommended approach we put in the attached "renewal_proposal_v2.pdf":

- Term: 12 months (Nov 15, 2026 — Nov 14, 2027)
- Committed capacity: 32 reserved GPUs (monthly billing cadence)
- Hardware mix (hybrid): 24 x H100, 8 x L40S. Rationale: H100s host the 6 high-priority slots where 95th/99th latency matters; L40S handles the bulk of medium-priority throughput where perf-per-dollar wins.
- Performance & econ summary (high level):
  - Aggregate throughput uplift vs 32 A100 baseline: ~1.5x observed at your batching distribution.
  - Estimated tokens-per-dollar improvement (blended): ~1.52x over A100 baseline for this workload mix (see hw_econ_backup.xlsx for model-level breakdown).
  - Monthly committed cost (blended): $303,200/month (compare to $288,000/month if staying all-A100 at list assumptions; blended gives better unit economics because L40S lowers incremental spend while preserving H100 tail improvements).
- Throughput SLA: We commit to a minimum tokens/sec per pool (documented in the proposal) with a 5% credit on missed SLOs. SLA applies to reserved capacity only.
- Canary & rollback: Proposed canary schedule attached (canary_plan.md). We will validate KV cache behavior, tail latencies, and ingestion pipelines during the staged rollout. If we hit a regression beyond agreed thresholds, we will pause and fallback to the previous mix or temporarily burst A100 capacity.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, countersign the proposal PDF and return it to me.
2) We will schedule the canary window the two-week window after the contract is effective.
3) Marissa will update the scoping SOW and Neha will confirm SLA metrics for the contract language.

Thanks — happy to hop on another call to walk through the hw_econ_backup workbook line-by-line.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(attachment: renewal_proposal_v2.pdf, hw_econ_backup.xlsx, canary_plan.md)
